_about: Plain-language definition of each KPI: what it measures and why it matters. Aliases inherit the definition of the KPI they point to. Read by export_to_prototype.py into DCTData.plant.kpi[ID].def; shown on R-01 KPI Reference.
OPS-001: How much saleable output the plant made against what the production plan called for in the month.
OPS-002: How much was sold against the sales volume planned for the month.
OPS-003: How much of the installed capacity was turned into good output; shows spare or stretched capacity.
PLT-001: Share of all calendar hours the equipment was actually running.
PLT-002: Overall equipment effectiveness: good output as a share of what the line could ideally make, combining availability, speed and quality losses.
PLT-004: Share of the valuable content in the feed that the process recovers into product.
PLT-005: Share of feed material that comes out as good, saleable output.
REL-001: Mean time between failures: average run hours between breakdowns. Higher means more reliable equipment.
REL-002: Mean time to repair: average hours to restore equipment after a breakdown.
REL-003: Hours of production lost to stoppages that were not planned.
REL-004: Tonnes of output lost because equipment was down when it should have been running.
REL-005: Share of scheduled preventive-maintenance jobs completed on time.
CST-001: Total production cost (variable plus fixed) for each tonne of good output.
CST-002: Costs that move with production volume: raw materials, power, fuel and consumables.
CST-003: Spend on fuel in the month.
CST-004: Power cost for each tonne of good output.
CST-005: Costs that do not move with volume (staff, rent, fixed maintenance), summed since April.
SUS-001: Volume of water drawn for operations in the month.
SUS-002: Greenhouse-gas emissions from operations, in tonnes of CO2 equivalent.
SUS-003: Energy used for each tonne of good output; lower means more energy-efficient production.
SIG-001: Hours of production lost to stoppages that were not planned.
SIG-004: Average number of days customers pay later than their agreed payment terms.
SIG-005: Number of customers more than 30 days overdue on payment.
SIG-006: Early warning that the business consumed more cash than operations generated in the month.
SIG-007: Tonnes of planned output threatened by current plant, supply or maintenance issues.
SIG-008: Number of open critical alerts about plant condition.
SIG-009: Number of critical materials at risk of running short before the next delivery.
SIG-010: Single-source suppliers whose stock cover is shorter than their resupply lead time.
SIG-011: Budget value of capex projects flagged as at risk of overrun or delay.
SIG-012: Share of customer dispatches that left late.
SIG-013: How far realised selling prices are running below plan, graded Low, Medium or High.
SIG-014: Month-on-month change in the main raw-material price index.
SIG-016: Number of supply lanes currently flagged as disrupted.
SIG-017: Month-on-month change in fuel cost per tonne of output.
SIG-018: Month-on-month change in power cost per tonne of output.
SIG-021: Number of breaches of environmental permits or limits.
EHS-001: Total recordable injury rate: recordable injuries per 200,000 hours worked (about 100 people for a year).
EHS-002: Number of incidents classed as high severity.
EHS-003: Events that could have caused harm but did not; a leading indicator of safety risk.
EHS-004: Number of incidents classed as critical to safety.
EHS-005: Number of times environmental limits were exceeded.
EHS-006: EHS corrective actions raised and not yet closed.
EHS-007: EHS corrective actions past their due date.
EHS-008: Number of EHS escalation deadlines currently counting down.
EHS-009: Share of EHS investigations due this month that were completed.
EHS-010: Share of EHS investigations due since April that were completed.
REG-001: Regulatory filings due and not yet submitted.
REG-002: Regulatory deadlines that fall in the next 30 days.
REG-003: Licences that expire in the next 12 months.
REG-004: Regulatory obligations that fall due in the next 30 days.
REG-005: Regulatory obligations already past their due date.
REG-006: Days until the earliest licence or permit expires at any plant.
REG-007: Actions required by regulators that are still open.
REG-008: Compliance actions past their due date.
REG-009: Whether an event that must be disclosed to regulators or the market is open.
REG-010: Number of regulatory breaches since April.
REG-011: Hours left before the nearest open disclosure deadline.
FIN-001: Earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation since April: core operating profit.
FIN-002: Earnings before interest and tax since April: operating profit after depreciation.
FIN-004: Cash generated by the business after operating costs and capex since April.
FIN-005: Return on capital employed: annualised operating profit as a share of the capital tied up in the business.
FIN-006: Borrowings less cash held; what the business owes net of its cash.
FIN-007: Economic profit since April: after-tax operating profit minus the cost of the capital used. Positive means value is being created.
FIN-008: Share of EBITDA that turned into free cash flow since April.
CSH-002: Cash freed up since April by working-capital and other cash initiatives.
CSH-003: Average cash collected from customers per day in the month.
CSH-004: Days between paying suppliers and collecting from customers (DSO + inventory days − DPO). Shorter frees cash.
CSH-006: Cash an entity must send up to the Group that its available cash does not cover.
WCP-001: Days sales outstanding: how many days of revenue are waiting to be collected from customers.
WCP-002: Days payables outstanding: how many days of spend are owed to suppliers.
WCP-003: How many days of production cost are held as inventory.
WCP-004: Cash tied up in operations: receivables plus inventory minus payables.
WCP-005: Change in net working capital on last month; positive means more cash tied up.
WCP-006: Net working capital expressed as days of revenue.
LIQ-001: How many months cash and undrawn facilities would cover fixed costs, overheads and debt service.
LIQ-002: How far leverage (net debt ÷ annualised EBITDA) sits below the lenders' covenant limit, as a share of the limit.
LIQ-003: Debt that must be repaid or refinanced in the next 12 months.
LIQ-004: Debt on floating interest rates, exposed to rate rises.
TRS-001: Foreign-currency exposure not covered by hedges.
TRS-002: How closely hedge value changes offset the value changes of the items they protect.
TRS-003: Share of the unhedged foreign-currency exposure that is in US dollars.
TRS-004: Share of forecast foreign-currency flows over the next 6 months already hedged.
TRS-005: Rupee impact of a 5% move in the US dollar on the unhedged exposure.
CPX-001: Capital-expenditure budget approved for the year.
CPX-002: Capex committed through orders and contracts to date.
CPX-004: Physical completion of capex projects, weighted by each project's budget.
PRG-001: Number of capex projects in each status (on track, at risk, delayed).
PRG-002: Share of planned programme benefits actually delivered since April.
PRG-003: Number of capex projects running behind schedule.
PRG-005: Number of transformation initiatives in each status.
STR-002: Share of planned transformation milestones completed.
VAL-001: EBITDA improvement delivered by value-creation initiatives since April.
VAL-002: Cash improvement delivered by value-creation initiatives since April.
VAL-003: Cost savings delivered by initiatives since April.
SUP-001: Share of purchase-order lines suppliers delivered on time.
SUP-002: Share of the ordered quantity suppliers actually delivered.
SUP-003: Share of received quantity rejected for quality.
SUP-004: How much actual supplier lead times exceed planned lead times, as a percentage.
SUP-005: Number of critical suppliers with no alternative source.
SUP-006: Average days late per contractor milestone due.
SUP-007: Share of supplier spend that goes to single-source suppliers.
SUP-008: EHS incidents involving suppliers or contractors since April.
CON-001: Contracts that expire in the next 90 days.
CON-002: Share of active contracts fully meeting their terms.
CTL-002: Internal-control tests that failed since April.
CTL-003: Assurance reviews completed since April, against the number planned.
CTL-005: Approved departures from policy since April.
CTL-006: Purchases from vendors not on the approved list since April.
CTL-007: Cases since April where one person held duties that should be split.
CTL-008: Access to systems or data by people not authorised, since April.
CTL-009: Data shared outside agreed rules since April.
CTL-010: Manual overrides of operational or system controls since April.
GOV-001: KPI certification approvals past their due date.
GOV-002: KPI values manually overridden instead of taken from source.
GOV-003: Data-quality issues that keep coming back.
GOV-005: Assurance actions past their due date.
GOV-006: Audit findings raised again after being closed before.
GOV-007: Leadership KPIs whose reliability is affected by an open finding.
GOV-008: Share of required evidence items that have been provided.
GOV-009: Average days taken to close audit findings since April.
TRU-001: Share of reported leadership KPI values that have been certified.
TRU-002: Number of reported leadership KPI values not yet certified.
TRU-003: Gap between the EBITDA in the Board pack and the certified EBITDA.
TRU-004: Reconciliation breaks between systems not yet resolved.
TRU-005: Share of reported leadership KPI values covered by the certification process.
TRU-007: Open reconciliation breaks large enough to be material.
TRU-008: Share of records loaded to the data lake that reconcile to the source system.
TRU-009: Share of flash-report lines that match the MIS.
TRU-010: Gap between flash revenue and closed revenue.
TRU-011: The largest gap, across entities, between Board-pack EBITDA and certified EBITDA.
EFF-006: Alerts where no owner has accepted responsibility.
EFF-008: Average days from raising an alert to resolving it.
EFF-009: Escalations closed in the last 30 days.
EFF-010: Issues that recurred in the last 90 days.
EFF-011: Root causes eliminated since April, against those identified.
PRD-001: Forecast days until the first plant misses its production plan.
PRD-002: Forecast chance that next month's output falls below plan.
PRD-003: Forecast gap between expected and planned EBITDA for the rest of the year.
PRD-004: Forecast cash shortfall over the next 90 days, if any.
PRD-005: Whether forecast leverage breaches the lenders' covenant limit.
PRD-006: Forecast output lost to downtime next month.
PRD-007: Forecast chance that OEE falls below 78% next month.
PRD-008: Forecast gap between full-year free cash flow and plan.
PRD-009: Forecast return on capital employed at year end (P12).
PRD-010: Revenue since April per full-time employee.
PRD-011: Good output per full-time employee in the month.
PRD-012: Forecast chance that full-year EBITDA misses plan.
